## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore `--wait` as a deprecated alias before merge: the parser now rejects it, so existing invocations fail even though the new ADR says the alias stays for one release.

## Changes
The pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` and keeps the default of 30. It also updates the parser tests, adds ADR `docs/adr/007-timeout.md`, and adds a root-level `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Accept `--wait` as a deprecated alias of `--timeout` — `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with status 2 ("unrecognized arguments") because `--wait` is no longer registered. `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5` says "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." — Every existing script that passes `--wait` breaks immediately, with no deprecation period or warning. — Fix: Register `--wait` as its own argument with `dest="timeout"` and a custom action that emits the deprecation warning, then extend `test_explicit_options` in `tests/test_cli.py` to cover it.
